newsitem.title: USA: U S West asks court to stay FCC order.
newsitem.headline: U S West asks court to stay FCC order.

text.p: U S West Inc said on Tuesday it asked a federal court to stay a substantial part of the Federal Communications Commission order implementing the 1996 Telecommunications Act.

U S West said in a statement that it faced "irreparable harm" if it were not allowed to negotiate the terms of interconnection with other telecommunications providers as the 1996 telecommunications act provided.
The FCC earlier on Tuesday rejected requests by three local telephone companies, including U S West, to set aside new rules designed to break open the local phone market to competition.

"We are disappointed by the FCC's failure to recognize the detrimental impact its order has and will continue to have on competition and the interconnection negotiation process," Mark Roelling, vice president of the company's legal department, said in a statement. "Faced with below-cost default proxy prices and a 'most favored nation' requirement, no company would be able to negotiate effectively with competitors."
